mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 1 Series M140i engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series M140i engine replacement typically costs £3,500-£8,500 for a reconditioned or rebuilt B58 unit supply-only. With supply and fit, expect £5,000-£10,000 depending on the specialist and location. A forged B58R engine build from a specialist can cost £8,610+ including labour. Main dealer new engine quotes can exceed £14,000 for parts alone.

mainEntity.name: What engine is in the BMW M140i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW M140i (F20/F21, 2016-2019) is powered by a 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six petrol engine with the engine code B58B30. It produces 340 hp (250 kW) at 5,500 rpm and 500 Nm of torque from 1,500-4,500 rpm. The B58 features a single twin-scroll turbocharger, Valvetronic variable valve lift, direct injection and an aluminium crankcase.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW M140i engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - the B58 engine in the BMW M140i is widely regarded as one of BMW's most reliable modern engines. Unlike the N20 and N47, timing chain failure is not a known widespread issue on the B58. However, early production examples (2016-2018) can suffer from oil pump drive gear failure due to plastic components in the oil pump chain guide. Common issues include coolant leaks, valve cover gasket wear and VANOS solenoid failure on higher-mileage cars.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 1 Series M140i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series M140i engine replacement typically takes 2-4 days for a specialist to complete, including removal of the old B58 unit and fitting the replacement. One specialist estimates labour time at approximately 15 hours. The complexity of the six-cylinder turbo engine means labour time is higher than for four-cylinder models.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW M140i and M135i?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the BMW M140i and M135i are performance models of the 1 Series, but they use different engines. The M135i (2012-2016) uses the N55 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six producing 320 hp, while the M140i (2016-2019) uses the B58 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six producing 340 hp.

mainEntity.name: Does a BMW 1 Series M140i rebuilt engine come with a warranty?

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 1 Series M140i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW M140i was launched in the summer of 2016 as the flagship performance model of the second-generation 1 Series, replacing the M135i. Powered by BMW's all-new B58 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six producing 340 hp, it represented the pinnacle of the rear-wheel-drive hatchback era. With 500 Nm of torque, a 0-62 mph time of just 4.6 seconds (automatic) and the legendary chassis balance of the F20/F21, the M140i remains one of the most celebrated modern BMWs. Production ran from 2016 to 2019 across the F20 (five-door) and F21 (three-door) body styles.

milestones.description: B58B30M0, 3.0L single twin-scroll turbo straight-six, 340 hp (250 kW), launched with the F20 five-door and F21 three-door 1 Series
Optional xDrive all-wheel drive introduced alongside rear-wheel drive
Shadow Edition models introduced with extended black exterior styling
Production continues; B58 engine now well-established as one of BMW's most reliable six-cylinders
F20/F21 generation ends; the M140i badge is retired and replaced by the front-wheel-drive 128ti and M135i xDrive on the F40 platform

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 1 Series M140i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 1 Series M140i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: H3: The BMW 1 Series M140i is powered exclusively by the B58B30 engine - a 3.0-litre single twin-scroll turbocharged straight-six that produces 340 hp and 500 Nm of torque. The B58 is widely regarded as one of BMW's most reliable modern engines, with far fewer major failure points than the N54 and fewer issues than the early N55. However, early production examples (2016-2018) have a well-documented weakness: the oil pump drive system. Coolant leaks, valve cover gasket wear and VANOS solenoid issues are also reported on higher-mileage cars. Replacement demand for the BMW M140i is relatively low compared to four-cylinder BMWs, but when failures occur, the cost of repair can be significant. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Oil Pump Drive Gear Failure - The B58's Early Production Weakness
problems.rootCause: Early production B58 engines (2016-2018) used plastic components in the oil pump chain guide and tensioner. Under normal operating stress, these plastic parts can break, throwing off the tension on the oil pump chain and leading to inconsistent oil flow. A distinctive humming or whining noise from the engine, especially during cold starts, is the primary warning sign. If the oil pump fails, oil pressure drops rapidly, and the engine can suffer catastrophic damage within minutes.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil pump drive gear, chain guide and tensioner with updated components
repairOptions.longevity: If humming/whining noise is detected early

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded oil pump components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If oil pump failure has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2016-2019 BMW 1 Series M140i is currently valued at approximately £12,000-£22,000 depending on mileage, condition and specification. This places the M140i firmly in the bracket where a rebuilt engine is a viable investment - replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value. For well-maintained, lower-mileage examples worth £16,000+, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with warranty is a sound investment.
problems.recommendation: If your B58-powered M140i produces a humming or whining noise from the engine on cold start, have the oil pump drive system inspected immediately. Early detection can prevent catastrophic engine failure. BMW has repaired this issue under warranty for many affected vehicles, but if your car is out of warranty, a specialist repair is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. For owners planning to keep their M140i for the long term, upgrading to an aftermarket metal oil pump drive gear is a worthwhile preventative measure.

problems.h4: Coolant Leaks - Reservoir Cap and Charge-Cooler Issues
problems.affectedModels: BMW 1 Series M140i (B58B30, all production years)
problems.rootCause: The B58 engine can be prone to coolant leaks. Problems with the coolant reservoir cap seals can bleed coolant slowly, whereas if the leak is heavy, check the charge-cooler hasn't been punctured. There are two coolant tanks on the M140i - one for the engine and a smaller one for the charge cooler.

repairOptions.longevity: If heavy leak or puncture detected

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new components
repairOptions.longevity: If overheating has caused significant damage

problems.recommendation: Coolant leaks on the B58 are usually repairable without engine replacement. If you see a "Coolant Low" message, investigate immediately. Start with the simplest fix - a faulty expansion cap is a common and cheap cause. Later cars came with rock guards to prevent radiator punctures from stones, so check if your car has these fitted.

problems.group: Valve Cover Gasket & VANOS Solenoid Wear
problems.h4: Valve Cover Gasket & VANOS Solenoid Wear - High-Mileage B58 Issues
problems.affectedModels: BMW 1 Series M140i (B58B30, higher-mileage examples, 60,000-100,000 miles)
problems.rootCause: The B58's valve cover gasket can degrade over time due to high engine temperatures, leading to oil leaks that can create a burning smell and, in severe cases, pose a fire hazard. VANOS solenoids can also fail due to oil contamination or wear, leading to rough idling, loss of power and increased fuel consumption.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve cover gasket and PCV components

repairOptions.longevity: If VANOS-related fault codes are present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new components

problems.recommendation: Valve cover gasket and VANOS issues on the B58 are usually repairable without engine replacement. A diagnostic scan will identify if VANOS codes are present. Address oil leaks promptly - a £400-£650 specialist repair is far cheaper than dealing with the consequences of a major oil leak. Unlike the N20, the B58 does not have widespread timing chain issues, making it a more dependable choice for long-term ownership.

problems.h4: Injector & PCV Diaphragm Failure - Known B58 Niggles
problems.affectedModels: BMW 1 Series M140i (B58B30, all production years)
problems.typicalFailureMileage: Variable - injector issues are not mileage-dependent
problems.rootCause: The B58's injectors can fail, with issues seemingly unrelated to mileage. The PCV (Positive Crankcase Ventilation) diaphragm can also fail, causing rough running and potentially a whistling noise. The PCV diaphragm is a cheap and easy DIY fix.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new components

problems.recommendation: PCV diaphragm failure is a cheap and easy fix - many owners have reported fixing it themselves for under £20. Injector issues should be diagnosed with a proper scan; replace faulty units individually rather than assuming the worst.
